risks.note: The Chairman's own diagnosis of the business names 'price erosion in generic molecules, lower export mix, below-industry-average margins, operational inefficiencies, higher fixed costs and elevated debt' as the current issues facing the Company, and the MD adds that pricing pressure in generic products 'will remain part of the operating landscape'. The MD separately concedes that a large part of the formulations business is still oriented toward generic solo products — so realised margin depends on a mix shift to differentiated combinations that has not yet happened.
risks.risk: Price erosion in generic molecules and a portfolio still weighted to generic solo products

risks.note: Management describes FY26 as a year of 'raw material price volatility' and 'supply chain disruptions', and lists input cost volatility among the challenges expected to persist. The stated cost response — selective backward integration, automation, process redesign and reduced import dependence — is itself an admission of current exposure. The BRSR flags raw materials, quality and supply chain management as a material risk with negative financial implications, on the grounds that substandard inputs or non-compliant supply chains can impair product quality, safety and long-term sustainability.
risks.risk: Raw material price volatility and import dependence in the supply chain

risks.note: The BRSR lists Regulatory Compliance as a material risk with negative financial implications: non-compliance may cause operational disruption, financial penalties and reputational loss. The Directors' Report cites 'changing regulatory requirements' as a factor in the challenging operating environment, and the MD lists regulatory risks among the persistent challenges. For an agrochemical maker whose growth plan runs through registrations (three TIM technical, fifteen me-too formulation and ten international registrations secured, twenty-plus more filed), registration timing and rule changes are directly load-bearing on revenue.
risks.risk: Regulatory compliance risk across product registrations and environmental/chemical regulation

risks.note: The Directors' Report states that 'Demand in the sector continued to be impacted by agricultural cycles, monsoon patterns, crop conditions, and farmer sentiment' — meaning a large part of revenue is exposed to weather and rural cash-flow conditions the Company cannot influence. Domestic retail grew only 5%, in line with industry.
risks.risk: Agricultural cycle, monsoon and farmer-sentiment dependence of end demand

risks.note: The global agrochemical market declined roughly 7% to USD 77 billion with broad-based regional contraction, and India's agrochemical exports fell 3% to USD 4.2 billion. NACL's export recovery leaned on a small number of products and geographies — normalisation of Propiconazole and Tricyclazole volumes on South American destocking, technical engagement in Vietnam and formulation-led growth in Africa — so the export engine, and the Key Accounts framework behind it, is concentrated in a handful of molecules and markets.
risks.risk: Export-market and geographic concentration exposure in a contracting global agrochemical market

risks.note: The BRSR names Waste Management and Climate Change (Emissions, Energy) as material risks with negative financial implications: inadequate waste management may cause non-compliance, legal liabilities, penalties and adverse impacts on surrounding communities, while evolving emission norms may force operational modifications and higher compliance costs. Mitigation runs through ZLD systems at Srikakulam and Ethakota, an incinerator and a newly inaugurated Effluent Treatment Plant — capital the Company must keep spending to hold its licence to operate.
risks.risk: Environmental, waste and emissions exposure inherent to technical-grade chemical manufacturing

risks.note: The BRSR identifies Health and Safety as a material risk: unsafe working conditions can cause occupational incidents, reputational damage, higher medical costs and operational disruption, mitigated by statutory adherence, EHS management systems, training, audits and a Zero Harm policy across sites. The Company reports zero TRIR in FY26 and five consecutive years of zero incidents, which describes present performance in what it itself calls 'a high-risk industry' rather than removing the exposure.
risks.risk: Process-safety and occupational health risk at chemical sites

risks.note: The Company entered FY26 with elevated debt and below-industry-average margins; the recovery rests on a Rs 250 crore rights issue, debt consolidation (borrowings down ~24%, zero long-term debt, debt-equity 0.93 to 0.44) and a rating upgrade, all achieved in the first year under new ownership. The Chairman states that synergy benefits from Coromandel 'will accrue progressively' and that FY26 laid only 'useful early foundations' — so the margin and cost thesis depends on integration outcomes that have not yet been demonstrated, while no dividend was recommended as the Company is in the early phase of turnaround.
risks.risk: Turnaround execution, leverage history and dependence on Coromandel synergies

sk.overview: The agrochemicals (crop protection) industry covers the development, manufacture and distribution of insecticides, herbicides, fungicides and plant growth regulators in Formulations and Technicals form. Per the issuer-commissioned ICRA Report (February 2026), the sector is supported by resilient Indian agriculture (healthy reservoir levels, robust crop production sustaining rural demand), a global 'China+1' shift favouring Indian chemical manufacturing, and sustained government fiscal support to agriculture and manufacturing.
